title: Deterministic failback proxy for shadowed A/B commits with replay buffer
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a deterministic failback proxy that ensures reproducible rollback behavior for shadow-to-canary promotions; includes a configurable replay buffer and deterministic session mapping. No API surface changes for customers.
body:
Context and motivation: We observed non-deterministic outcomes during shadow-to-canary promotions when the promoted variant failed and the system attempted automatic fallback. This produced unreproducible post-mortems and flaky smoke tests. This PR introduces a deterministic failback proxy that (1) records a lightweight replay buffer for shadow traffic, (2) replays requests deterministically during failback, and (3) enforces transactional unwind semantics when rollback triggers. The goal is to make automatic rollbacks reproducible and safe across canary/A-B promotions without changing public APIs.

Design summary: The proxy sits in the staged-promote path and maintains a per-cohort deterministic session map (hash of request fingerprint + cohort seed) to route replayed traffic in the exact order seen during shadow capture. A bounded circular replay buffer persists only metadata and KV cache snapshots (not full payloads) to keep costs low. On failback, the proxy transitions to replay mode which streams buffered entries into the target older model instance(s) with backpressure-aware pacing to avoid overload. The proxy supports manual dry-run replay and an automated rollback path that coordinates with the rollout conductor to mark the promotion as reverted and to attach the replay transcript to the rollout audit.

Implementation highlights: - New package redwood/rollout/failbackproxy implementing Proxy, Recorder, and Replayer abstractions. - Replay buffer is implemented as append-only ring using RocksDB (sharded by cohort id) with a TTL and size quota per cohort. - Added deterministic session mapping util (rollout/hash_session.go) used by the traffic router. - Extensions to rollout controller API to emit replay-ready audit events (no external API change). - Instrumentation: per-cohort replay size, replay duration histogram, deterministic-entropy-score metric for drift detection. - Unit and integration tests for deterministic ordering, buffer eviction, and transactional unwind.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by ENG-1423 stakeholders. - [x] Unit tests covering Recorder/Replayer edge cases. - [x] Integration test exercising a simulated promotion -> fail -> automated replay -> successful revert. - [x] Metrics and dashboards added (dashboard JSON in observability-pack). - [x] Manual dry-run exercised on staging cluster.

Commits (summary): - 0d3f1c8 add failbackproxy package and basic recorder/replayer interfaces - a9b12f4 implement deterministic session mapping and ring buffer backed by RocksDB - b5c4e21 integrate proxy with rollout controller audit events - 7f1d9aa add metrics and observability dashboard - c2a7ef0 tests: deterministic ordering, eviction, transactional unwind - f9d3b44 docs: rollout runbook updates and dry-run instructions

Changed files (high level): - redwood/rollout/failbackproxy/proxy.go - redwood/rollout/failbackproxy/recorder.go - redwood/rollout/failbackproxy/replayer.go - redwood/rollout/hash_session.go - redwood/rollout/replay_ring/rocks_ring.go - redwood/rollout/controller_integration.go - observability-pack/dashboards/failback-replay.json - docs/runbooks/failback-replay.md - tests/integration/failback_replay_test.go - go.mod, go.sum (dependency on github.com/google/uuid and rocksdb bindings)

Review conversation (high level): - Daniel Kim (reviewer): "This looks good overall; two main asks: add a migration safety check for existing DB shards and ensure the RocksDB options are tuned for low tail-latency under high-write pressure." Author reply (Priya Shah): "Added migration safety check (rocks_migrate.go) and benchmark-tuned options in rocks_ring.go; noted in comments why specific settings were chosen and linked to perf runs." - Aisha Patel: "Can we make the replay buffer TTL configurable per deployment and expose it in the Dedicated config? Also add a feature flag to gate the automated replay path." Author reply: "Made TTL a deploy-time config with sane defaults; added rollouts.features.enable_failback_replay feature flag and a console toggle entry in rollout settings." - Mateo Ruiz: "Tests look comprehensive but I'm concerned about interaction with autoscaling during replay. Please add a test that simulates scale events mid-replay." Author reply: "Added integration test that triggers a scaledown event and validates replay backpressure preserves ordering and resumes when capacity returns."

CI checks: - unit-tests (pass) - integration-tests (pass) - lint (pass) - gosec (pass) - infra/deploy (flaky on first run, successful on rerun)

Post-merge actions: - Ops runbook updated with step-by-step failback drill and checklist. - Observability: dashboard deployed to staging and production's beta tenants. - Follow-up: ENG-1499 to add optional payload redaction for GDPR sensitive snippets during replay.

Merge outcome: Squash and merge. No release blocking CI failures. Rollout will be gated behind the feature flag and enabled in a targeted cohort for the next staged promotion.

Notes for oncall: If an automatic replay starts and causes increased latency, toggle rollouts.features.enable_failback_replay to false in the console and open a rollout revert ticket. Replay transcripts are attached to rollout audit entries for root-cause analysis.
